title: Further Thoughts on "Sea Change"
summary:
Wallace,
Sir John Templeton had warned that when investors say times are different,
it's usually in an effort to rationalize valuations that appear high relative to history. Recent events have shown that the risk of rising inflation can't
be ignored in perpetuity. It causes things to be built that otherwise wouldn't have been built,
investments to be made that otherwise wouldn't have been made,
and risks to be born that otherwise wouldn't have been accepted.

thesis: The speaker argues that the investment environment has undergone a sweeping alteration due to a fundamental shift from ultra-low interest rates to a new norm of higher rates, which invalidates strategies that succeeded between 2009 and 2021. This change is driven by the end of accommodative central bank policies and the reawakening of inflationary psychology, making it unlikely that the previous era of perpetual prosperity and declining rates will continue.
